# lumos_entitlement_approval_workflow (Resource)

Turns on an entitlement's approval workflow override, binding an approval template (a `lumos_workflow` of type `approval`) in place of the app's. Destroying this resource turns the override off, so the entitlement uses its app's approval workflow again. It doesn't delete the template.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Turns on the entitlement's approval workflow override with its own approval
# template. Destroying this resource turns the override off; to stop managing
# it without turning it off, use a removed block (see below).
resource "lumos_entitlement_approval_workflow" "this" {
  entitlement_id = lumos_entitlement.deploy_admin.id
  workflow_id    = lumos_workflow.admin_approvals.id
}

# Stop managing the binding without changing Lumos.
# removed {
#   from = lumos_entitlement_approval_workflow.this
#   lifecycle {
#     destroy = false
#   }
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `entitlement_id` (String) The entitlement's ID, which `GET /v1/entitlements` and `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/entitlements` return as `id`. Requires replacement if changed.
- `workflow_id` (String) UUID of the workflow to associate.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = lumos_entitlement_approval_workflow.this
  id = "<entitlement id>"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import lumos_entitlement_approval_workflow.this "<entitlement id>"
```
